q: A consignor had deposited the wagon registration fee with his indent, but the Railways failed to supply wagons against the indent. In such a case, the wagon registration fee deposited by the consignor is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways
options.B: Adjusted against the demurrage payable by other consignors
options.C: Credited to sundry other earnings
options.D: Refunded to the consignor

q: A passenger who bought an unreserved ticket but did not travel asks for his money back as a matter of course. In regard to refund on unreserved (UTS) tickets, the correct position is that:

options.A: Full refund is admissible at any station at any time
options.B: Refund can be granted only by the Railway Claims Tribunal
options.C: Refund is ordinarily not admissible, except in specified circumstances such as cancellation of the train
options.D: Refund is admissible on deduction of the prescribed cancellation charge in all cases

q:
A probationer is asked to distinguish the two broad families of railway statistics. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. Financial statistics are concerned with the money results of working, namely the earnings earned and the expenditure incurred.
2. Operating statistics are concerned with physical units of performance, such as train kilometres run, Net Tonne Kilometres performed and wagon days.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A consignor specifies in his Forwarding Note that his consignment should be carried by a particular route, although a shorter route is also available. Where the consignor so specifies the route, the freight is charged:

options.A: On the basis of the distance by the route so specified, even if it is longer than the shortest route
options.B: Always on the basis of the distance by the shortest route
options.C: On the basis of the route chosen by the destination station
options.D: At a flat rate irrespective of the distance

q: As distinguished from luggage kept in his own custody, luggage booked by a passenger on a luggage ticket is carried:

options.A: In the passenger's own custody, without any responsibility of the Railways
options.B: Only by the next train following the passenger's train
options.C: In the goods shed till it is claimed by the passenger
options.D: In the brake/luggage van of the train, the Railways being responsible for its safe carriage

q: A newly posted assistant in the Traffic Accounts Office is told that the Advice of Internal Check for a station is not a single combined document. The correct position is that it is prepared:

options.A: Separately for coaching accounts and for goods accounts
options.B: Jointly for coaching and goods accounts in one advice
options.C: Only for goods accounts, coaching being exempt
options.D: Only when the station itself demands it

q: During internal check it is found that a station collected more fare from the public than was due and the excess has to be returned. The document prepared by the Traffic Accounts Office for this purpose is the:

options.A: Error sheet
options.B: Overcharge sheet
options.C: Stock sheet
options.D: Advice of Payment

q: At the close of a month, a station has collected its earnings and despatched the remittance, but the amount has not yet been credited to the Railway's account. In traffic accounts this amount is correctly described as:

options.A: Traffic Suspense
options.B: Station imprest
options.C: Cash-in-Transit
options.D: Coaching outstanding

q: A trainee is sorting the earnings of through traffic for apportionment between two zonal railways. Which of the following is NOT taken up for apportionment?

options.A: Coaching earnings of through traffic
options.B: Goods earnings of through traffic
options.C: Parcel earnings of through traffic
options.D: Sundry other earnings

q: A booking clerk asks under which head the earnings from parcels, luggage and postal traffic should be classified. The correct classification is:

options.A: Other coaching earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Sundry other earnings
options.D: Capital receipts

q: A Station Master proposes to meet a petty station expense out of the day's collections and remit only the balance. In regard to station earnings, the correct position is that:

options.A: Petty expenses may freely be met out of station earnings
options.B: Station earnings must be remitted in full and cannot be appropriated for departmental expenditure
options.C: Half the earnings may be retained till the month-end
options.D: Earnings may be adjusted against dues of the station staff

q: Excess Fare Tickets collected by ticket checking staff during a drive are sent for check. This check is exercised in the:

options.A: Commercial Branch of the Division
options.B: Personnel Branch
options.C: Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: Railway Recruitment Board

q: A bundle of tickets is returned by a station as 'non-issued'. The Traffic Accounts Office checks these tickets mainly to ensure that:

options.A: Their printing quality is satisfactory
options.B: The fare printed on them is the latest fare
options.C: The ticket stock register is neatly maintained
options.D: Such tickets were in fact not sold or issued to passengers

q: Collected tickets received from stations are put through check in the Traffic Accounts Office primarily to ensure that:

options.A: All collected tickets are duly accounted for and none is missing or unaccounted
options.B: The handwriting of the collecting staff is legible
options.C: The paper used for the tickets is of good condition
options.D: The total number of passengers in the year can be counted

q: The statement of approximate gross earnings of Indian Railways, used for watching the earnings trend during the year, is compiled and issued every:

options.A: Day
options.B: Week
options.C: Month
options.D: 10 days

q: Two zonal railways carried a through consignment over different distances. The share of each railway in the earnings of that traffic, i.e. its apportioned earnings, is worked out on the basis of:

options.A: The cash collected at its own stations only
options.B: The suburban earnings of the railway
options.C: The amount surrendered to the Railway Board
options.D: The distance the traffic is carried over its system

q: The balance sheet of a railway shows a debit balance under 'Traffic Suspense'. Broadly, this indicates:

options.A: Traffic dues and outstanding earnings yet to be recovered or adjusted
options.B: Profit earned by the Traffic Department
options.C: Excess cash deposited by stations
options.D: Refunds payable to passengers

q: A Travelling Inspector of Accounts visiting stations is chiefly concerned with preventing loss of railway income. His primary function is to:

options.A: Prepare the station balance sheet
options.B: Inspect stations and prevent leakage of railway revenue
options.C: Compile the annual Appropriation Accounts
options.D: Sanction refunds of fares

q: A probationer asks whether the internal check in the Traffic Accounts Office covers only a small sample of station transactions. The correct position is that it is:

options.A: A test check of a small percentage of transactions
options.B: A check exercised by the statutory audit party
options.C: A detailed, cent per cent check of the accounts rendered
options.D: A check confined only to cash remittances

q: Debits and disallowances are advised to a station through the Advice of Internal Check, but the detailed error sheet has not yet reached the station. The station must take these debits to account:

options.A: Only after the error sheet is received
options.B: Only after confirmation from the Divisional Office
options.C: Only at the end of the financial year
options.D: Whether or not the error sheet has been received

q: A station clerk assumes that the Accounts Office Balance Sheet is prepared by each station for its own transactions. This is incorrect because that balance sheet is prepared:

options.A: In the Traffic Accounts Office, reflecting station balances as per the accounts office books
options.B: By the Railway Board for all zonal railways together
options.C: By the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during inspection
options.D: By the Divisional Commercial Manager

q: An operating officer has the Net Tonne Kilometres and the tonnes carried for a period and wants the average distance each tonne was carried. The average lead of goods traffic is computed as:

options.A: Train kilometres divided by the number of trains
options.B: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by tonnes carried
options.C: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by wagon kilometres
options.D: Earnings divided by tonnes carried

q: A diesel shed returns its fuel figures for statistical compilation. Specific Fuel Consumption on Indian Railways is expressed per:

options.A: 100 engine kilometres
options.B: 1000 Net Tonne Kilometres
options.C: 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres
options.D: 1000 train kilometres

q: For electric traction, Specific Energy Consumption is expressed as the electrical energy consumed per:

options.A: 100 train kilometres
options.B: 1000 Net Tonne Kilometres
options.C: Engine hour
options.D: 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres

q: A wagon is loaded, travels to destination, is unloaded and is again placed for loading. The time taken between its two successive loadings, expressed in days, is known as:

options.A: Wagon turn-round
options.B: Terminal detention
options.C: Average lead
options.D: Engine day

q: A freight customer wants to track the movement of his rake in real time. The system that primarily provides real-time information on freight operations, including rake and wagon movements, is:

options.A: The Passenger Reservation System
options.B: The Freight Operations Information System
options.C: The Unreserved Ticketing System
options.D: The National Train Enquiry System

q: A reservation supervisor is asked to name the computer software on which the Passenger Reservation System operates. It is known as:

options.A: UTS
options.B: TAMS
options.C: CONCERT
options.D: FOIS

q: The information systems such as PRS and FOIS used on Indian Railways have been developed and are maintained by:

options.A: Rail India Technical and Economic Service
options.B: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation
options.C: RailTel Corporation of India
options.D: Centre for Railway Information Systems

q: A passenger wishes to book an unreserved ticket on his phone without visiting the station. The mobile application provided by Indian Railways for this purpose is:

options.A: UTS on Mobile
options.B: IRCTC Rail Connect
options.C: FOIS Mobile
options.D: National Train Enquiry System

q:
Consider the following statements about Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevaks:
1. The sevaks are authorised agents who sell unreserved tickets from premises outside the station.
2. The sevaks earn a commission on the tickets sold by them, while the fare collected is a coaching earning of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A consignee presents himself at the destination goods shed and demands his consignment without any document. Delivery of goods at the destination is normally given:

options.A: To any person who asks for the goods
options.B: Only to the consignor in person
options.C: Only after the expiry of the free time
options.D: On surrender of the Railway Receipt by the consignee or his endorsee

q: A consignor is offered a choice between the owner's risk rate and the railway risk rate for his consignment. As compared with the railway risk rate, the freight at owner's risk rate is:

options.A: Lower
options.B: Higher
options.C: Equal
options.D: Exactly double

q: A trader's goods were entrusted to the Railways and later lost. Under Section 106 of the Railways Act, 1989, his claim for compensation or for refund of an overcharge must be preferred in writing within:

options.A: Three months from the date of entrustment of the goods
options.B: Six months from the date of entrustment of the goods
options.C: One year from the date of entrustment of the goods
options.D: Two years from the date of entrustment of the goods

q: A claimant's case for compensation for non-delivery of goods is not settled by the railway administration. He can take the claim before the:

options.A: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission only
options.B: Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: Railway Claims Tribunal
options.D: Comptroller and Auditor General

q: A zonal railway's working expenses and gross earnings are placed before a finance officer. The Operating Ratio of the railway represents:

options.A: Net revenue expressed as a percentage of the capital-at-charge
options.B: Goods earnings expressed as a percentage of total earnings
options.C: Capital expenditure expressed as a percentage of revenue expenditure
options.D: Working expenses expressed as a percentage of gross earnings

q: A costing study compares Net Tonne Kilometres with Gross Tonne Kilometres of goods working. The ratio of NTKM to GTKM indicates:

options.A: The proportion of the total load hauled which is revenue-earning, paying load
options.B: The speed of goods trains
options.C: The density of traffic on the line
options.D: The proportion of empty wagons in the wagon fleet

q: A traffic costing officer separates the cost of hauling traffic between terminals from the costs incurred at the terminals themselves. The cost of hauling traffic between terminals, excluding terminal costs, is called:

options.A: Fully distributed cost
options.B: Line haul cost
options.C: Terminal cost
options.D: Joint cost

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fully distributed cost allocates the fixed and overhead costs also to the individual services.
2. Marginal or variable cost takes into account only those costs which vary with the volume of traffic.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements about unclaimed consignments:
1. Unclaimed consignments are destroyed after the expiry of the prescribed period.
2. Unclaimed consignments are disposed of by public auction after due notice, and the sale proceeds are applied first towards the dues of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A consignee has lost his Railway Receipt and the receipt is not forthcoming. Delivery of the consignment may be given to him:

options.A: Without any formality
options.B: Only after the expiry of one year
options.C: Only after the goods are auctioned
options.D: Against an indemnity bond executed by the claimant

q:
Consider the following statements about station cash remittances:
1. Every remittance of cash from a station to the cash office or bank is accompanied by a cash remittance note.
2. Credits for station remittances are afforded in the accounts solely on the basis of the station's own statement, without any acknowledgement of the bank or the cash office.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: At the end of a ticket-checking drive, a squad leader asks under which head the fare and excess charge collected from passengers found without proper tickets will be accounted. They are credited to:

options.A: Sundry other earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Miscellaneous receipts of the division
options.D: Coaching earnings

q: A passenger is found travelling in a higher class than the one for which he holds a ticket. The ticket checking staff realise from him:

options.A: The full fare of the higher class afresh
options.B: Only the reservation charge of the higher class
options.C: The difference of fare between the class held and the class travelled in, together with the excess charge
options.D: A fixed penalty irrespective of the distance travelled

q:
Consider the following statements about catering earnings:
1. In a departmental catering unit, the sale proceeds are receipts of the Railways.
2. In a licensed catering unit, the sale proceeds belong to the licensee and only the licence fee is an earning of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements about goods outstandings at a station:
1. They include 'to-pay' freight which has not yet been collected.
2. They also include wharfage and demurrage which have accrued but have not yet been realised.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A zonal railway carries out the monthly reconciliation of earnings between the Commercial and Accounts departments primarily to:

options.A: Agree the statistical, approximate earnings with the earnings actually brought to account and investigate the differences
options.B: Fix the earnings targets for the next month
options.C: Allot rakes and wagons to divisions
options.D: Decide the postings of commercial staff

q: For accounts purposes, the final monthly earnings of a zonal railway are taken as:

options.A: The approximate figures issued every ten days
options.B: The earnings brought to account by the Traffic Accounts Office after internal check
options.C: The figures furnished by stations without any check
options.D: The Budget Estimates of earnings for the month

q: A long-distance passenger notices that his through fare is less than the sum of the fares for each part of the journey. This is because passenger fares for through journeys are charged on the telescopic principle, which means that:

options.A: A flat fare is charged irrespective of the distance travelled
options.B: The rate per kilometre decreases as the distance of the journey increases
options.C: The fare is the sum of the separate fares for each railway traversed
options.D: The fare increases in direct proportion to the square of the distance

q: A passenger cancels a confirmed Premium Tatkal ticket and claims a refund of the fare. The correct position is that:

options.A: Full fare is refunded without any deduction
options.B: Fare is refunded after deduction of clerkage charges only
options.C: Fifty per cent of the fare is refunded
options.D: No refund is admissible on cancellation of the ticket

q:
Consider the following statements about a licence of railway land:
1. Licence fee received for the use of railway land is accounted as a goods earning.
2. A licence of railway land gives the licensee only a permission to use the land and does not create any tenancy or leasehold interest in his favour.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A season ticket holder claims a reserved berth in a long-distance train on the strength of his season ticket alone. The correct position is that a season ticket entitles the holder to travel:

options.A: In a reserved berth in any train of his choice
options.B: Only in the brake van of passenger trains
options.C: In the unreserved accommodation of the class and over the section for which the ticket is issued, and does not by itself entitle him to a reserved berth or seat
options.D: In the first class of all trains, irrespective of the class of the season ticket

q: A station has to make a small official payment locally, but the Station Master is told he cannot touch the day's ticket collections for it. Petty official payments required to be made at a station are met:

options.A: Out of the earnings collected at the station, before their remittance
options.B: From the personal funds of the Station Master in all cases
options.C: Only after obtaining cash from the Railway Board for each payment
options.D: From the cash imprest held at the station for the purpose, which is recouped on rendering the paid vouchers

q: A passenger booked a reserved ticket at one PRS counter and later seeks its cancellation at a different station altogether. A reserved ticket issued at a computerised (PRS) reservation counter can be cancelled:

options.A: Only at the same counter at which it was booked
options.B: At any computerised reservation counter, and not necessarily at the counter or station of booking
options.C: Only at the destination station of the journey
options.D: Only through the Railway Claims Tribunal

q: An industrial concern wants the siding serving its factory to be worked by the Railways on agreed terms. A private siding on the Railways is worked:

options.A: Without any agreement, at the discretion of the Station Master
options.B: Under an agreement with the State Government in whose area it is situated
options.C: Only under an order of the Railway Claims Tribunal
options.D: Under an agreement executed between the Railways and the siding owner, which lays down the terms relating to its working, charges and maintenance

q: A student applies for a concessional season ticket for his daily travel to college. Concessional season tickets for students are issued for travel:

options.A: Between the student's residence and the educational institution attended by him
options.B: Over the entire railway system without any restriction
options.C: Only between two suburban stations of the same city in all cases
options.D: Only for travel during the examination days

q: A person is found hawking eatables without authority inside a train and another is found begging on the platform. Under the Railways Act, unauthorised hawking and begging in a train or in any part of the railway premises are:

options.A: Permitted on payment of a licence fee to the Station Master
options.B: Permitted only in unreserved coaches
options.C: Prohibited, and are punishable offences
options.D: Treated as earnings activities of the Railways

q: A publisher despatched bundles of magazines by a passenger train for distribution in another city. Newspapers and magazines offered for carriage by passenger trains are treated on the Railways as:

options.A: Goods traffic carried only by goods trains
options.B: Parcel traffic, booked on parcel way bills and charged at the parcel scales
options.C: Free traffic for which no charges are recovered
options.D: Luggage of the passengers travelling by the train

q: A loader stuffs a wagon well beyond its permissible carrying capacity and the excess is detected. Under Section 73 of the Railways Act, 1989, where a person loads a wagon beyond its permissible carrying capacity, the railway administration may recover from him:

options.A: Only the normal freight for the excess weight loaded
options.B: Wharfage for detention of the wagon at the station
options.C: Punitive charges for overloading the wagon, in addition to the freight due
options.D: The cost of repairs to the wagon

q: Before handing over a consignment, the destination station suspects that its weight and class have been understated at booking. Before delivery of a consignment, the railway administration is empowered under Section 78 of the Railways Act, 1989 to:

options.A: Sell the consignment by public auction
options.B: Re-weigh, re-measure or re-classify the consignment and recover the charges found due on such re-check
options.C: Refuse to accept all future consignments of the party
options.D: Confiscate the consignment to the Railways

q:
Consider the following statements about platform tickets:
1. A platform ticket is valid for two hours from the time of its issue.
2. The fare paid for an unused platform ticket is refunded to the purchaser on surrender of the ticket.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A reservation clerk explains that, apart from the general and emergency quotas, many long-distance trains carry a separate quota of reserved accommodation earmarked for allotment to:

options.A: Season ticket holders
options.B: Holders of free passes
options.C: Press correspondents only
options.D: Foreign tourists holding a valid passport and visa

q:
Consider the following statements about fare concession to Divyangjan passengers:
1. Concession in rail fares is admissible to Divyangjan passengers (such as the orthopaedically handicapped and the visually impaired) on production of the prescribed certificate.
2. An escort accompanying such a Divyangjan passenger is also eligible for concession in fare.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A parking contractor who wins an earning contract at a station deposits earnest money with his tender. The earnest money deposited by the successful tenderer for an earning contract at a station, such as a parking or advertisement contract, is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways in all cases
options.B: Adjusted towards, or retained as, security for the due performance of the contract
options.C: Refunded to him on the very day the contract is awarded
options.D: Treated as a traffic earning of the station

q:
Consider the following statements about Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway:
1. The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway are confined to the traffic which originates on that railway.
2. The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway include the Net Tonne Kilometres arising from through traffic carried over the lines of that railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A shed master points out that shunting work yields no tonne kilometres against which fuel use can be measured. For shunting services, where the output cannot be measured in tonne kilometres, the specific fuel consumption is worked out with reference to:

options.A: The number of wagons shunted during the period
options.B: The gross tonne kilometres of the trains formed
options.C: The shunting engine hours performed
options.D: The number of shunting staff employed

q: A parcel is very bulky although its actual weight is small, and the booking clerk charges it on a weight higher than the scale shows. In parcel traffic, where a parcel is bulky in relation to its actual weight, the parcel charges are levied on the basis of:

options.A: The actual weight of the parcel alone
options.B: A flat rate per parcel, irrespective of weight
options.C: The declared value of the contents
options.D: The volumetric (measurement) weight of the parcel, where it exceeds the actual weight

q: A passenger travelling on a Tatkal ticket is asked by the ticket checking staff to prove his identity. A passenger travelling on a Tatkal ticket is required to:

options.A: Carry and produce one of the prescribed original photo identity proofs during the journey
options.B: Obtain the permission of the Station Master before starting the journey
options.C: Travel only in the unreserved class
options.D: Surrender the ticket at the destination station in all cases

q: A passenger who booked an e-ticket through IRCTC travels without taking a printout of it and is questioned on the train. In respect of an e-ticket booked through IRCTC, the correct position is that:

options.A: A printout of the ticket obtained from a PRS counter is compulsory for travel
options.B: The ticket must be got validated at the booking station before travel
options.C: E-tickets are valid only for travel in unreserved classes
options.D: The Electronic Reservation Slip, or the reservation message received on the mobile phone, along with the prescribed identity proof, is itself the authority to travel and a printout is not compulsory

q: A rake of specially converted wagons is loaded entirely with cars at an automobile hub. NMG (New Modified Goods) wagons on Indian Railways are primarily used for the carriage of:

options.A: Coal in bulk
options.B: Automobiles and motor vehicles
options.C: Liquid petroleum products in bulk
options.D: Foodgrains in bulk

q: A local artisan is allotted a small outlet at a station to sell the handloom products of his region under a railway scheme. The 'One Station One Product' (OSOP) scheme of Indian Railways provides for:

options.A: Appointment of one catering contractor for all the stations of a division
options.B: Sale of tickets of only one class at a station
options.C: Allotment of stalls/outlets at stations for the display and sale of local and indigenous products of the region
options.D: Booking of only one commodity at every goods shed

q: A zonal headquarters sets up a special unit to meet chambers of commerce and scout for new freight business. Business Development Units (BDUs) have been set up on Indian Railways at the zonal and divisional levels primarily to:

options.A: Conduct departmental examinations of commercial staff
options.B: Verify the accounts rendered by stations
options.C: Tap new streams of freight traffic and maintain liaison with trade and industry
options.D: Manufacture and repair freight wagons

q: A passenger with a reserved ticket gets down midway of his own accord and later demands money back for the part of the journey he did not perform. A passenger who, of his own accord, discontinues his journey midway on a reserved ticket is, in regard to the untravelled portion of the journey:

options.A: Entitled to a full refund of the fare
options.B: Ordinarily not entitled to any refund
options.C: Entitled to a refund of fare less the cancellation charges
options.D: Entitled to a free ticket for the return journey

q:
Consider the following statements about booking of perishable consignments:
1. Freight charges on consignments of a perishable nature are required to be prepaid at the time of booking.
2. Perishable consignments can be booked on 'to-pay' terms in the same manner as ordinary goods traffic.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A consignor offers a consignment of explosives and asks that it be sent by the fastest passenger train. Explosives offered for carriage by rail are accepted:

options.A: By passenger trains, if loaded in the guard's brake van
options.B: By any train, without any special conditions
options.C: Only by goods trains, subject to the conditions laid down in the Red Tariff
options.D: Only in unreserved coaches of passenger trains

q: A station asks how frequently the consolidated result of the internal check of its accounts reaches it. The Advice of Internal Check in respect of the accounts of a station is issued by the Traffic Accounts Office:

options.A: Every week, after the weekly check of station returns
options.B: Every month, after the check of the station's monthly balance sheet and returns
options.C: Once a year, at the close of the financial year
options.D: Only in a month in which an inspection of the station is carried out

q: A probationer asks how the Travelling Inspector of Accounts covers the accounts of the period since his last visit, instead of checking every month in full. During his inspection of a station, the Travelling Inspector of Accounts ordinarily exercises:

options.A: No check of accounts, his inspection being confined to the verification of cash
options.B: A complete check of the accounts of all the twelve months since the last inspection
options.C: A check only of the goods accounts, the coaching accounts being excluded
options.D: A complete check of the accounts of one selected month and a test check of the accounts of the other months

q: A consignment of currency notes sent by the Reserve Bank of India is loaded for despatch under guard. Consignments of currency notes and other valuables (treasure) tendered by Government or the Reserve Bank of India are carried by the Railways:

options.A: In ordinary parcel vans, along with other parcels
options.B: In special treasure vans/coaches, under proper escort and on payment of the prescribed charges
options.C: Only by road, under railway escort
options.D: Free of charge, as departmental traffic

q: A merchant returns the empty drums and gunny bags in which his goods had arrived, for carriage back to the forwarding point. Empty packages, such as drums, cylinders and gunny bags, which had earlier been carried by rail as the packing of goods and are returned by the consignee, are carried by the Railways:

options.A: At the same rates as the loaded packages
options.B: Only when loaded in passenger trains
options.C: At concessional (reduced) freight rates, subject to the prescribed conditions
options.D: Free of charge in all cases

q: A patient who must travel repeatedly to a distant hospital for treatment seeks a fare concession. Concession in rail fares for travel in connection with medical treatment is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: All patients suffering from any ailment whatsoever
options.B: Only patients referred by a Government hospital
